notes.title: One of your most requested interface features has arrived: customizable text scaling is now available in The King is Watching!

items.text: The new setting lets you adjust the size of tooltips and most in-game text. Text scaling has a more limited range on Steam Deck, where certain boundaries remain in place to preserve readability on its smaller display.

We’ve also added a tooltip delay setting. This lets you choose how quickly tooltips appear while moving your cursor across the kingdom or navigating with a controller, helping reduce visual flickering.
Alongside these interface additions, the update includes several gameplay, animation and tooltip fixes. Full patch notes are available below:
Added a Text Scale setting that controls the size of tooltips and most in-game text (its effect is more limited on Steam Deck to preserve readability).
Added a Tooltip Delay setting to reduce screen flickering when moving the cursor across the kingdom or navigating with a controller.
Drunken Dwarves now prefer throwing their mugs at targets that are not already affected by intoxication.
Building animation speeds now more accurately reflect their production speeds.
Improved the Merchant Advisor’s ability tooltip after all charges have been used.
Fixed an issue that could prevent Smokeeye from using his abilities correctly when the player entered a wave with only temporarily Banished units on the battlefield.
Fixed Endless Mode rewards sometimes being granted in the wrong order.
Fixed Advisor portraits in Upgrade Tree tooltips occasionally displaying the wrong animation frame.
Fixed the Magic Prism artifact triggering spells in the wrong position.
Fixed the building movement overlay not appearing when hovering over certain parts of a building.
Thank you for all the feedback you’ve shared about the new interface. We’ll continue refining the experience as you put these new settings to use!
— Hypnohead Team

Updated numerous localized strings for better clarity, particularly in Simplified Chinese and Russian.
Updated font files to include missing Japanese and Chinese characters.
Fixed a rare crash that could occur when entering run preparation.
Fixed various UI layout issues.
Fixed an issue where quickly opening and closing the Rewards screen could prevent reward cards from receiving gamepad focus.

We've added a new setting that lets you choose your preferred control scheme when playing on Steam Deck.
Gamepad Only — Uses the familiar control scheme found in most console games. This is now the default setting and will be selected automatically.
Cursor Only — Takes advantage of Steam Deck's unique hardware controls, including its trackpads and rear buttons.
Combined — Allows you to use both control schemes simultaneously. This was the previously active setting.

Some players reported confusing behavior on Steam Deck, including flickering UI elements and controls that didn't always feel intuitive. This was caused by the game automatically switching between control schemes when detecting different types of input. To make things more predictable, we've made Gamepad Only the new default and turned Combined into an option that players can deliberately enable.
If you prefer using both control schemes and are comfortable with the game switching between them on the fly, you can still select Combined.
You can switch between all three modes at any time in the game's Settings menu.
Thank you for your continued feedback and support! We're looking forward to bringing you more UI improvements in the next updates.

items.text: The gates to the Shifting Sands now stand open.

Available now as a free update for all owners of The King Is Watching, the Shifting Sands expansion brings a wealth of new content to the realm. Customize your adventures with Danger Modifiers, face new bosses and enemies, discover powerful artifacts and spells, experiment in the new Free Reign Mode, and enjoy improvements to Endless Mode, progression, balance, and overall gameplay.
Before you march your troops into the dunes, watch the launch trailer and witness the wonders (and horrors) that await beyond the shifting horizon:

The Shifting Sands – a brand-new map where ancient magic pulls enemies, bosses, and events from all previously conquered lands into a single realm. Shape each run with 36 Danger Modifiers and face four new bosses, the mysterious Fennec tribe, and other desert horrors.
King Personas – unlock cosmetic appearances to give your rulers a fresh and regal look.
3 new dwarven units and 2 advisors to strengthen your kingdom and expand your strategic options.
10 new artifacts offering powerful effects and new build possibilities.
3 new spells added to your royal grimoire.
Improved Endless Mode with wave rewards and enhanced difficulty scaling.
Free Reign Mode – use Danger Modifiers on any map to create your own challenges and adventures.
Onboarding and progression improvements for newly crowned kings.
Numerous balance changes and quality-of-life improvements across the realm.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44827188/8242dee23863b9a1f8a63ba663b939d137127686.gif"]

Before we delve into the latest affairs of the realm, a brief reminder: the official Hydragoose plushie remains available for pre-order. Should your court be in need of a loyal guardian, vigilant overseer, or exceptionally regal honker, now is the time to secure one.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44827188/25b406cc85ba64d2ce66a98d43a68b911b626692.png"]

The Shifting Sands are no ordinary desert. Ancient magic twists space and time as rifts tear open across the dunes, drawing enemies and allies from distant lands and forgotten ages. Here, the past, present and future exist side by side beneath an eternal, unforgiving sun.

In the Shifting Sands, you may encounter enemies and events from any land you have already conquered. As always, a prophecy at the start of each run will reveal the boss awaiting you. It may be a familiar foe from your past campaigns or one of four new bosses created exclusively for this map. Only the Kraken remains absent, too immense even for the rifts of the Shifting Sands to drag from the Dark Realm. After all, even magic has its limits.

Endless Mode has a special place in our hearts.

While it may not be every king’s favorite pastime, those who embrace it often create builds so outrageous that even we never saw them coming. However, Endless Mode had its shortcomings: rewards stopped once you entered it, and enemy scaling eventually struggled to keep pace.

To address this, Endless Mode now grants rewards for clearing waves, just like the rest of your run. We have also reworked difficulty scaling. Enemy HP and Damage modifiers now increase with every wave, with their growth accelerating every 20 waves.

releases.displayName: Onboarding & Early Progression Improvements in the Free Shifting Sands Update

items.text: The royal court has carefully considered the counsel and feedback delivered by rulers across the realm. Today, we would like to present several improvements shaped directly by your voices — changes aimed primarily at easing the first steps of newly crowned monarchs, particularly during onboarding and the early stages of their reign. When the Shifting Sands conquest begins on June 11th, these changes will stand ready to guide new rulers on their journey.
Should you wish to revisit the chronicles that came before, the royal records may be found here:

[dynamiclink href="https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/2753900/view/681876878050460112"][dynamiclink href="https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/2753900/view/681876878050460949"][dynamiclink href="https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/2753900/view/719032209192779824"]
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44827188/1ba6ede407795c71f9bdedd06a0f00782c55865c.gif"]

We believe the game already does a solid job of explaining the basics, but the overall process of learning The King is Watching could still be improved in several ways. With that in mind, we dedicated additional time to refining the onboarding experience.

First, we expanded the tutorial. It now explains more mechanics that players will encounter throughout the game. The tutorial also features a proper ending, including a special boss encounter designed to introduce both the tone of the game and the structure of a full run.
Additionally, Threat Tier 0 will now feature only one boss instead of two. This should make first runs shorter and allow players to unlock upgrades more quickly.

The upgrade system itself has also been revised. Most notably, the Yellow Eye Upgrade tree has changed. You no longer need to spend Town Denarii to unlock these upgrades. Instead, they are earned by completing each level on Threat Tiers 1, 2, and 3.

notes.title: The progression logic is now more intuitive

items.text: Easier-to-use buildings are unlocked first for each Tier on every map
Artifacts and spells follow afterward
The final unlocks usually contain buildings that are more specialized or require stronger synergies
We also rebalanced the Red Eye Upgrade tree. Banishing and Re-Rolling upgrades now have separate branches, allowing you to unlock these abilities earlier in your progression.
Added extra unlocks to both branches
Increased the number of banishes gained per upgrade from 1 to 3
Reorganized several upgrade unlock orders - for example, you can now banish Nobles and unlock additional building slots earlier than before.
Finally, we adjusted map progression. New maps are now unlocked by completing the previous map on Threat Tier 1.
We hope these changes make onboarding smoother, clearer, and more enjoyable for both new and returning Kings.

We shall soon return with the final royal chronicle covering the Shifting Sands update. According to our court mages and trusted advisors, the tidings yet to come should prove especially exciting for both newly crowned rulers and seasoned monarchs alike.
— Hypnohead Team

items.text: As the dunes continue to shift beyond the borders of the kingdom, whispers of dark new adversaries reach the royal court. Today, our loyal mages present a glimpse into the dangers awaiting your conquest in the lands of Shifting Sands.
Those seeking knowledge from past royal chronicles may find the previous Shifting Sands update article here:
[dynamiclink href="https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/2753900/view/681876878050460112"]
The Desert itself is home to four new bosses who may rise to challenge your reign.
Behold: Monkey King, Greedscale, Matriarch of Dragons, Goruk, The Chainbound, and Drentlyr, Ancient Leshen.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44827188/3f89354f26d7177a1e6bd6724d1e89ee6b8c973d.gif"]

He is not evil — merely rebellious. And he has little love for any man bold enough to climb his mountain and call himself king. Only he is king here, and the monkeys follow him with unwavering devotion. Well, as much devotion as monkeys are capable of.

A master of trickery, the Monkey King floods the battlefield with illusions, making it difficult to distinguish real danger from distraction. While your gaze shifts between false threats and moving shadows, his devoted monkeys slip into your kingdom to wreak havoc on your economy and defenses.
Watch closely, Your Highness. The moment you lose sight of the true threat, the Monkey King has already won.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44827188/1880b3f2a5398c7208cabe3c1edc67b976e128d6.gif"]
Long before you raised your banners here, the forest had its own ruler. Old and patient, Drentlyr nurtured and guarded the woods for centuries.

Unfortunately, your royal construction plans required wood — and a great deal of it. Every tree felled and every stump left behind was an offense against the forest. Its ancient protector followed the trail of axes all the way into the Shifting Sands.

Even where no forest should exist, the Ancient Leshen bends nature to his will, shaping towering Ents to tear down your fortifications. He seeks no tribute and offers no bargains. Only vengeance. Your kingdom must fall so that something greener may grow upon its ruins.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44827188/b29f50ab4d7c5b58bc22d58c88507d21d9a2be8a.gif"]
Every fire-spitting lizard, winged terror, and treasure-hoarding wyrm can trace its bloodline back to her. She has heard tales of your kingdom. More importantly, she has heard of your treasure.

The Matriarch is the oldest, greediest, and most fearsome of her kind. She believes all gold belongs beneath her claws. She does not invade for conquest, vengeance, or glory. She comes to claim every shining thing she can carry — and burn whatever remains.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44827188/20a22709f4ebc62a2799aff1546679c355d8e485.gif"]
Once, he was nothing more than a prisoner — a giant goblin buried beneath layers of iron and stone. Then he escaped.
But the prison never released him.
Chains, cages, shackles, and locks fused to his body and followed wherever he walked, clinging to him like a curse.

Now Goruk marches toward your kingdom to bind every living thing in iron. Peasants, soldiers, workers — none shall escape his chains. To him, your kingdom is merely another prison waiting for its bars.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44827188/5f2a065ec2575a1c6e4f8842cb2632b0f59a731c.gif"]

The Fennecs are a tribe that dates back to times immemorial. According to some royal historians and sages, the tribe originated from the possession of the lost wanderers with the spirits of the desert. What other explanation can there be about a tribe that boasts a host of knights, mages, and cavalry that can give any kingdom in the realm a tough run but leaves nothing in its wake except the ruins of its temporary camp

The leading edge of their army consists of highly trained fencers who fight with the precision of hired mercenaries of the Free Cities. Alone, these swordsmen are fearsome. Paired up with the Magi of the Fennecs, however, that unleash raw power of fire, they are deadly.

There are also the Javelin Masters, ranged fighters who are skilled at throwing javelins which are almost as long as a horse. While you pray for victory, your soldiers pray for the luck for these long javelins to miss or at least impale their neighbors instead. Then comes the cavalry which rides in with fury, breaking up the ranks and tearing straight through your backlines to create chaos in place of organized firing lines. And if that’s not enough, Fennec Knights will finish the job, challenging your mightiest champions that will stay alive long enough for them to arrive on the battlefield.

Though Fennecs are not the only ones that don’t like your presence in Shifting Sands. Jugs, Sand Worms and Sand Slimes will chew through your troops in order to sate their hunger. And their hunger is neverending, unlike your potential rule!
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44827188/fc3f17f1e20b75f7147bf61e4e43667eee1e626b.gif"]

While Shifting Sands will reintroduce events familiar from other maps, we have also prepared over a dozen new, unique encounters exclusive to this region. Here are some of the challenges and curiosities awaiting your kingdom:

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44827188/e3be18e832306a5670e0288b7c230c0a0238d789.png"][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44827188/107a38822eca31d5f643afa445d6f67b88925ca1.png"][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44827188/f240dfcf33825223c849cb095dad3f6c17780cd0.png"][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44827188/ecf2dbbcc716d700d77d6fd30dc86ae2d7832e30.png"]
A silver-tongued cult leader arrives at court, promising enlightenment through the sacred Eye,
Concern grows within the royal court after an advisor was overheard explaining his work-related stress to a cat
A mysterious omen emerges in the skies above the kingdom.
That is all for today, Noble Kings.
May your banners fly proudly over the dunes.
— Hypnohead Team

Below you can find the full update notes. But before you go into reading them, we wanted to let you know that we've launched our first merchandise line - it's six different T-Shirts you may buy at tinyBuild shop, operated by our partners from Tinybox.

The Dark Realm is a dark and dangerous map. It’s inspired by the works of Lovecraft and is centered around the theme of cosmic horrors. Here you will face The Kraken and its deadly tentacles.

This map brings new dynamics, since enemies stay out of your reality and invisible to your armies. Only by focusing your Royal Gaze upon a specific building you may attack them. So you are free to choose the right time to cleanse the waves of eldritch offspring
Four new bosses were added to the map
O’Chtulpus

The Kraken will be a unique boss that plays completely differently from anything you’ve faced before. We really wanted it to feel like you’re slaying a true eldritch monstrosity - one piece at a time. Don’t prepare for a blitz - prepare for a prolonged siege. Defeating it will take longer than any other boss in the game, so to keep the overall playtime within reasonable limits, we decided to skip Tier 2 bosses on this map entirely. The Kraken will summon troops and retreat into hiding until you’ve dealt with them all. Its HP bar is longer than a highway, and its attacks can one-shot your troops if you’re not careful. Stay sharp.

The map will feature tentacles as main enemies. They do not march like goblins. They do not swarm like undead. Some wait motionless until you get close and others set to work spawning living bombs. Some evolve into siege tendrils and others combine with corrupted souls to create spell-casting hybrids to attack your troops.
You may ignore a few, you will not ignore all.

This update introduces a new category of buildings: Offensive Structures. Existing buildings such as Tesla Tower, Cannon, and Balloon Bomber Hangar have been moved into this category. In addition, six new structures have been added:
Timber Launcher. Launches a wooden log at an incoming enemy.
Fuel Launcher. Launches a fuel barrel at incoming enemies.
Great Slingshot. Attacks incoming enemies with a giant stone.
Firebomb launcher. Launches napalm bombs at incoming enemies.
Poison Tower. Attacks incoming enemies with a beam of light that poisons them, dealing damage over time.
Dovecote. Releases several birds that circle over the battlefield and poop on enemies.

We’ve also rebalanced the damage and economy of the offensive structures, so you can use them more efficiently. Some upgrades further help with this. E.g., one of Poison Tower’s upgrades, will allow you to extract fuel from killed enemies.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44827188/5d917f1b5e3a5464224483bd98d65d6d2448cd90.png"]
We’ve also added a new Elite Unit: Cannons. It’s similar to Catapults and Ballistas in terms of long ranged attacks, but its trait increases the damage of all Offensive Structures.
We’re also introducing several quality-of-life improvements in this update.
First two are delivered as two unlockable upgrades.

To unlock the next map you still need to beat Threat level 3 on the previous map. Beating a Threat level automatically collects all Ascension crystals from lower Threat levels on that location. Starting from Threat level 6 each you would need to beat levels 6-10 on each location separately.
We hope the above change will allow you to enjoy new maps faster. Also we made a slight changes to Threat level modifiers order, Second boss mod appears on Threat level 6 instead of 5.

releases.displayName: New Bosses Coming In Volcano Update

items.text: As you may have heard, the royal gaze is turning toward the blazing horizon — our next major content expansion, the Volcano Update, is in the works! In the coming weeks, we’ll be sharing a series of royal decrees detailing the update’s new content:
The new bosses who will challenge your rule,
The mechanics and rewards that make the Volcano a new and unique battlefield,
The enemies and events that will test your leadership and strength,
And the game-wide improvements arriving alongside the update.

Work on the update continues as our alchemists, engineers, and scribes labor around the clock to ensure the realm’s next expansion is worthy of your crown. But today, we begin with the most fearsome of them all — the Bosses of the Volcano.

notes.title: The Lords of Ash and Flame

items.text: These are not mere foes. They are living disasters — legends, bound by neither mercy nor reason. Defeating them is the challenge for even most skilled rulers.
[img src="https://i.ibb.co/gFQ9fQKJ/Ignahog.gif"]

From the burning slopes of the volcano strides Ignahog, the colossal Boar-Titan said to embody the fury of the Cinderwilds. His molten veins glow beneath cracked armor-plating of stone, and each breath escapes as a cloud of smoke and cinder.

Though titanic in size, Ignahog never fights alone - smaller hogs scamper ahead, sabotaging supply lines, scouting, and performing tricks no one expects from, well… hogs. When Ignahog charges, the ground itself rebels, splitting into rivers of lava. It is said the volcano answers his call not out of loyalty, but out of shared hatred for all things soft, fragile, and flammable.
Facing Ignahog is not a battle — it’s a natural disaster.
[img src="https://i.ibb.co/VWPzSfVw/Sniper.gif"]

When brute force fails, the Scarlet Goblins summon Smokeeye, their mercenary sharpshooter infamous across the land. His oversized rifle — welded together from stolen pieces of three different nations — spits death from unseen distances.

Smokeeye is a phantom, vanishing into thick smoke the moment danger nears. But he is no mere gunman: he’s a cunning engineer, constructing makeshift outposts in the blink of an eye. Once he accepts a contract, he won’t stop until his target falls. And as long as Smokeeye draws breath, your army will bleed one soldier at a time.
[img src="https://i.ibb.co/vvP8HkqK/Phoenix-1.gif"]

High above the infernal plains soars Ashfeather, a fiery titan revered by the Scarlet Goblin pantheon. His wings ignite the air into shimmering heat waves, grilling soldiers alive beneath their armor - a cruel inversion of the usual cook-and-be-cooked dynamic.

Ashfeather has existed for eons, reborn endlessly from his own flame. Whether slain or simply bored of his current form, he immolates and reforms anew, each rebirth sharpening his wrath. Your invasion of goblin lands has disturbed his sacred sleep — and he intends to remind the living that fire does not forgive.
[img src="https://i.ibb.co/hRvZRQNg/Spider.gif"]
Forged in the molten pits of the Inferno itself, Skarkh is the spider-born avatar of the Demon of Rage — half machine, half monster, all fury.

He covers the battlefield in smoldering webs that burst into flame at his command, turning the ground into a maze of molten death. His broodlings - explosive spiderlings of chitin and hate - scuttle toward your troops and detonate in suicidal glee. To fight Skarkh is to fight Rage made manifest: a creature that burns through metal, web, and flesh alike.
[img src="https://i.ibb.co/FkmdVW4Y/Goblodancer.gif"]
Once an unremarkable goblin drummer with no sense of rhythm, Goblark became a monstrous symphony of destruction after being force-fed demon blood by his kin.

Now towering above the battlefield, he dances to his own maddening beat — twin scythes slicing arcs of crimson through the smoke, his massive bell-helm tolling with every strike. Each toll freezes hearts; each swing drives both ally and enemy into frenzy. Fueled by endless infernal adrenaline, Goblark fights without pause — and drags everyone else into his rhythm.
When the bell tolls, it tolls for all.
[img src="https://i.ibb.co/N6NxNQyK/Worm.gif"]

From the volcanic depths slithers Solvurm, an ancient flame worm whose breath turns stone to slag. His titanic body tunnels beneath the battlefield, bursting forth in pillars of living fire. Each wound he suffers births new horrors — molten offspring spawned through parasitic means best left unspoken.

To slay Solvurm is not a single victory but a brutal ritual — a slow dismemberment of a living wildfire. You must sever him piece by piece until his monstrous form stops writhing. Entire cities have burned trying. And now, your kingdom is next on his list.

These six terrors are only the beginning. Each boss in the Volcano update brings not just a fight, but a set of modifiers you will have to beat on higher difficulties with some requiring extra aerial defence towers or creation of additional stockpiles of resources.

In our next royal address, we’ll share more details about the map’s unique mechanics, rewards, and the changing nature of the volcano itself. Stay tuned, and keep your armies ready — the ground beneath your castle is beginning to rumble.
Until next time, Kings —
~ The Hypnohead Team

notes.title: A Kingdom Off to a Glorious Start

items.text: It’s been just a few weeks since The King is Watching launched, and we’re overwhelmed with the response. Many of you have already poured countless hours into the game, conquered high Threat Levels, and shared your wild, creative builds with us. Your enthusiasm has been nothing short of inspiring, and it makes us even more determined to keep building upon this world: more content, more Kings, more units.
But before expanding the kingdom, we need to strengthen its foundations.

Over the past weeks, we’ve mobilized everyone—seriously, everyone. We’ve spoken with nearly every GameMaker developer we could find, and we’re now in direct contact with the engine’s creators. Together, we’ve made huge strides in identifying technical issues, from crashes to performance. Some bugs still remain, but we’re confident that the new mid-run saving system is a massive step forward for the stability and playability of the game.

notes.title: That said, there are two big areas left to improve

items.text: ⚖️ Fixing critical balance issues
🛠️ Clarifying UI and core mechanics
We started with balance…and that leads us to Leo.
We’ll be honest: we didn’t balance King Leo the Wise properly. He was simply too strong. Here's why:
His first ability had an extremely short cooldown, enabling frequent blueprint sales.
Selling blueprints rapidly boosted morale, which in turn greatly increased unit damage and resource production.
Players could bypass early-game resource management entirely, a system that’s supposed to be a core part of the challenge.
On top of that, Leo has one of the best Gaze upgrades and can spawn free units on cooldown.

We want each King to offer unique bonuses and a meaningful challenge. Some will naturally be stronger than others. And we love seeing you break the game with wild builds, whether intentional or not. But Leo was on an entirely different level. Not just compared to existing Kings, but even those we’re planning to introduce in the future.

Trust us, we considered it. But buffing everything to match Leo would cause runaway stat inflation and break the balance of the game in other areas. It would also make it far harder to design future content. So a nerf was necessary.

We hate nerfing things. And our goal was to do it just once. But after reviewing your feedback, we agree: we went too far. This update includes a revised, more balanced version of Leo and several other changes to improve the experience overall.
King Leo the Wise’s third ability resource costs have been reverted:
1st use: Wheat 200, Wood 200 → Wheat 100, Wood 100
2nd use: Wheat 400, Wood 400 → Wheat 200, Wood 200
3rd use: Flour 250, Metal 250 → Flour 100, Metal 100
4th use: Flour 600, Metal 600 → Flour 300, Metal 300
First ability cooldown reduced from 40s → 30s.
Improved the functionality of artifacts applying productivity seals for Threat Level 8+ runs.
Added Steam achievements for completing the game on Threat Level 10 with each King.
Made various localization and text improvements across multiple languages.

We want to sincerely thank you for your feedback. Some of it was tough to read, but it showed just how passionate this community already is about The King is Watching. We share that passion with you, and we’re learning every day how to better shape this game together.
You’ve helped us learn a valuable lesson: don’t nerf that hard. We hope future updates will bring only joy, chaos, and crown-worthy moments.
~ Hypnohead
